# Task 86b: upload UI and reader wiring (repo LectorIA-meta, branch feat/upload-ui)

server/uploads or server/guard behaviour except where stated below.

  the strict regex in core/uploads.ts) by delegating to `loadUploadedBook(id)` from
  server/uploads/loader.ts. Shelf behaviour unchanged. Unknown or malformed ids
  still `notFound()`. Missing or expired uploads -> `notFound()`. Do NOT cache
  uploads in the module-level cache forever (a small bounded cache or none).

  with the exact button text "Bring your own key!". human_required -> ask to
  retry the check. expired/not_found -> say the upload expired, upload again.

  goes to BYOK. Update core/upload-policy.ts and free-book.ts (store a per-UTC-day
  count instead of a one-shot flag; it is a hint only, the server enforces).

  key) under a versioned key, capped at 20 entries, and show them on the home

  forgets locally. Drop entries the reader 404s on is NOT required.

  existing home CSS conventions and all six skins.

1|# Upload processing API
2|
3|Server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into reader data. The browser
4|parses the file with `core/epub.ts` and POSTs the sections; the server
5|cleans, segments, and classifies one chapter-part per call so every
6|request finishes inside the Hobby 60 s budget.
7|
8|## Create
9|
10|`POST /api/uploads`, JSON body:
11|
12|```json
13|{ "title": "Middlemarch", "author": "George Eliot", "sections": [RawSection], "turnstileToken": "…" }
14|```
15|
16|`sections` is the `RawSection[]` shape from `core/clean-types.ts`. Limits:
17|50k words free, 400k with a key; 600 sections; 20k chars per block; 4 MB
18|body. BYOK sends its key per call in the `x-byok-key` header (in memory
19|only, never stored). Needs same-origin JSON plus the Turnstile/human
20|cookie flow shared with chat and images.
21|
22|Success: `{ "status": "created", "id": "u-…", "chapters": 24, "parts": 24 }`.
23|The id is a 128-bit capability; free jobs also bind the anon cookie.
24|The cleaning judge gets 25 s inside this request; past that the book
25|keeps its deterministic chapters.
26|
27|## Step
28|
29|`POST /api/uploads/<id>/step`, body `{}` or `{ "chapter": 3 }` with an
30|optional `turnstileToken` when the human cookie expired. Processes the next
31|pending part (segment + emotion) and stores it. BYOK repeats the key header;
32|free repeats the cookies.
33|
34|- `{ "status": "working", "id": "u-…", "done": 3, "total": 24 }` — call again.
35|- `{ "status": "done", "id": "u-…", "done": 24, "total": 24, "costUsd": 0.021 }`
36|  — the analysis is assembled; `costUsd` is the real Meta+Jev cost.
37|
38|Re-driving a finished part or job is idempotent and free. Music needs no
39|step: scenes carry the same `final` emotion vectors Oz has, so the
40|existing track selection scores them unchanged.
41|
42|## Errors
43|
44|`{ "status": "error", "code": "<code>", "message": "…" }`. Codes: `too_long`
45|(use BYOK, 413), `daily_books_reached` (2/day, 429), `daily_budget_reached`
46|(503), `human_required` (403), `bad_request` (400), `unavailable` (503,
47|refunded), `not_found` (404), `expired` (30 days, 410).
48|
49|## Reading and cleanup
50|
51|`loadUploadedBook(id)` in `server/uploads/loader.ts` returns the
52|`BookPayload` the reader consumes (`{ book, scenes }`). Uploads expire
53|after 30 days; `GET /api/cron/cleanup-uploads` (Bearer `CRON_SECRET`,
54|daily) deletes their private blobs.
55|
56|## Storage
57|
58|Uploads live in a separate private Blob store, not the public image
59|store: a store's access mode is fixed at creation, so `access: "private"`
60|puts would fail against it. The token comes from
61|`UPLOADS_BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` (passed explicitly to every Blob call)
62|and the owner creates the store by hand. Without the token the routes
63|answer `unavailable`; they never fall back to the public store.

1|# Design: task 86 upload processing
2|
3|Goal: server path turning a browser-parsed EPUB into the same data a shelf
4|book has (`BookPayload`: book + analyzed scenes), behind free/BYOK caps, one
5|chapter-part per request so every call finishes under the 60 s Hobby budget.
6|
7|## API
8|
9|- `POST /api/uploads` — body `{title, author?, sections, turnstileToken?}`
10|  where `sections` is the browser's parsed EPUB sections (`RawSection[]`).
11|  Validates, cleans (deterministic + contributor judge), takes quota/spend
12|  (free only), stores `book.json` in private Blob, job state in Redis.
13|  Returns `{status:"created", id, chapters, parts}`.
14|- `POST /api/uploads/<id>/step` — body `{}` or `{chapter}`. Segments and
15|  classifies the next pending part (or that chapter's next part), stores the
16|  part result. Returns `{status:"working", id, done, total}` or
17|  `{status:"done", id, done, total, costUsd}` after finalizing.
18|- `GET /api/cron/cleanup-uploads` — deletes `uploads/` blobs older than 30
19|  days. Bearer `CRON_SECRET`, daily schedule in `vercel.json`.
20|
21|Full contract in `docs/uploads.md`. Reader entry: `loadUploadedBook(id)`
22|in `server/uploads/loader.ts` (wired into `server/books.ts` later, by owner).
23|
24|## Flow
25|
26|Create: same-origin + body cap + strict parse → env → Turnstile →
27|anon cookie → BYOK header? → deterministic clean + word count
28|(`too_long` past 50k free / 400k BYOK) → quota (2/day, IP or cookie) →
29|spend reserve ($0.25 flat, total + `upload:spend:daily` caps) → judge →
30|build book + textVersion → split parts (≤150 paras) → Blob + Redis.
31|
32|Step: guards as above → load job (free jobs bind the anon cookie, BYOK
33|jobs need the key header per call) → next pending part → Redis lock →
34|re-check part blob (idempotent, free) → segment via exported
35|`chapterPrompt`/`parseScenes` + `validateSceneCoverage` (one retry) →
36|classify each scene (Jev + `classifyScene` override when a server Jev key
37|exists, else contributor-only vector; per-scene errors keep `final: null`
38|like Oz) → store part → finalize under a guard when all parts land
39|(assign `c<ch>s<k>` ids, `validateBookCoverage`, `adjust` real spend).
40|
41|Music: Oz has no stored cluster at runtime; the reader scores each scene's
42|`final` vector against the manifest (`rankScored`). Uploads reuse that path
43|by producing the same `final` shape. No new music code.
44|
45|## Money and quota
46|
47|- `FREE_BOOKS_PER_PERSON = 2`, day in key, 48 h TTL (`server/guard/quota`).
48|- `UPLOAD_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_MICRO = 1_000_000`; total cap shared with
49|  images/chat via `reserveSpend` with a `dailyKey` override (defaults keep
50|  old behavior and tests).
51|- Refund exactly once on server failure via a `setNxEx` refund guard;
52|  user errors never take quota; abandoned jobs keep the reserve.
53|
54|## Trust
55|
56|Sections are untrusted: strict parse, caps on sections/blocks/chars, word
57|limits. Model calls have no tools and fixed prompts; output is clamped and
58|coverage-validated, emotion ids restricted to the 8. Every external call
59|has an `AbortSignal` timeout. Errors to the client are codes only; the
60|BYOK key stays in memory (header per call, never stored or logged).
61|
62|## Shortcuts
63|
64|- Part results are re-segmented from scratch when a step is retried after
65|  a route kill; the Blob-exists check is the only dedup.
66|- Meta/Jev retries keep the pipeline's fixed policy; a pathological retry
67|  storm can hit the route kill, and the client just re-drives the step.
68|- No resplit pass for uploads (Oz-only refinement).

Context: the EPUB upload on the home page is a client-side stub. `core/epub.ts` parses in the browser, `app/home/upload.tsx` + `core/upload-policy.ts` route free vs BYOK (`app/home/byok.tsx`), and after "Read with soundtrack" it says "coming soon". Build the server path that turns an uploaded book into the same data a shelf book has (book + analyzed scenes with emotion + music cluster), cheaply, safely, within Vercel Hobby function limits. Investigate the code yourself (pipeline/, core/, server/guard, server/images, server/chat, app/api). A separate UI task will consume your API; keep the API small and documented in a short comment block or docs/uploads.md.

## Owner decisions (fixed)
- Model: `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` through the existing Meta client (`pipeline/meta.ts`) for cleaning judge, segmentation and emotion. Emotion: use Jev (`pipeline/jev.ts`, pinned model per AGENTS.md) when a usable Jev key is configured on the server, with the existing Muse override for low confidence; otherwise contributor alone using the existing override/classification prompt (only the 8 ids; never fake an emotion; failures follow AGENTS.md rules). BYOK books use the user's Meta key for every Meta call and contributor-only emotion (no Jev on our key).
- No image generation, no music generation, no narration during processing. Music: map each scene's emotion to the existing music clusters exactly the way Oz's analysis does (find how Oz gets its cluster/track assignment and reuse that code).
- Free path limits: same as now, at most `FREE_BOOK_MAX_WORDS` (50k) words; reject larger with a clear error code that tells the client to use BYOK. Also cap chapters/paragraph lengths/total bytes defensively.
- Caps for the free path: at most 2 books per person per UTC day, counted on BOTH hashed IP (existing ipBucket/hashIp, IPv6 /64) and the signed anon cookie, whichever hits first, via the existing server/guard quota helpers (`takeDualQuota`/`refundDualQuota`; update the currently-unwired book quota hook in server/guard/quota.ts: 2 per day, day in the key, ~48h TTL). Global spend cap USD 1/day for uploads, via `reserveSpend` with a separate daily key such as `upload:spend:daily:<day>` (parametrize the key minimally and keep image/chat behavior and tests unchanged; uploads should still count toward the existing overall total cap). Make both numbers single named constants.
- Turnstile through the existing guard (`checkHuman` and the human cookie flow, same as chat/images). Same-origin check like PR #111 (`rejectsCrossSite`) and JSON content-type. Body read with `readBodyCapped`.
- Refund on failure: if processing fails for server-side reasons (Meta/Jev/Blob down, validation of model output impossible after retries), release the spend reservation and refund the person quota exactly once. A user-caused rejection (too long, bad input) never takes quota. An abandoned job may keep its reservation (conservative); say so in a comment.
- BYOK: skip quota and spend caps, still require same-origin + Turnstile + size limits (a much higher word limit is fine, e.g. 400k, constant). The key arrives in a request header per call, is used in memory only, never stored (not in Redis, Blob, logs, errors, job state).

## Design constraints
- Vercel Hobby: each request must finish well under 60s. Use a client-driven, resumable job: e.g. `POST /api/uploads` (validate, caps, store the parsed book in Blob, create job state in Redis with TTL, return an unguessable id and the chapter count), `POST /api/uploads/<id>/step` (process the next pending chapter or a given chapter idempotently: clean, segment, emotion; store the chapter result), and finalization when all chapters are done (assemble book + analysis in the exact shape the reader consumes, reconcile real spend with `adjust`, mark done). Re-calling a finished step must be idempotent and cost nothing. Pick the simplest design that works; if one chapter can exceed the time budget, split work (e.g. segment and classify in separate steps, or cap chapter size).
- Ids: 128-bit random (crypto), URL-safe, prefixed (e.g. `u-...`), validated with a strict regex on every route. The id is the capability; additionally bind the job to the anon cookie for free jobs so another browser cannot drive or burn someone else's job.
- Storage: Vercel Blob under `uploads/<id>/...`. The book text is the user's: never list uploads publicly, never return Blob URLs to the client; read via server only. Check whether the existing store supports `access: "private"`; if you can't tell, use public access with the unguessable id path and `addRandomSuffix` as appropriate, and note it. TTL: store createdAt; refuse to serve after 30 days, and add a cleanup that deletes expired `uploads/` (e.g. a cron route protected by `CRON_SECRET` with a daily Hobby-compatible schedule in vercel.json). Keep it small.
- Provide `server/uploads/...` with a loader the reader can use: `loadUploadedBook(id): Promise<BookPayload | null>` returning the same `BookPayload` shape as `server/books.ts` ({ book: {id,title,author,chapters,paragraphs,textVersion}, scenes: AnalyzedScene[] }). Another worker is building the generic `/read/[bookId]/[sceneId]` route right now in a separate worktree (its `server/books.ts` has `loadBook`/`loadBookData` with a LOADERS map); do NOT edit `server/books.ts` or app/read or app/leer in this task. I will wire the loader in after that lands.
- Pipeline reuse: reuse pipeline/ and core/ code (segment prompt + validation `validateSceneCoverage`, classify/override, clean judge, http timeouts/retries, prices). Pipeline files are fs-based and another worker has uncommitted edits in pipeline/segment.ts, classify.ts, ingest.ts, prices.ts: change those files as little as possible (adding `export` to an existing pure helper is fine; no restructuring or moving code). Put fs-free server orchestration in server/uploads/.
- Security: book text is untrusted input. Model calls: no tools, no secrets in prompts, structured JSON output parsed and validated with a schema (zod if already a dependency, otherwise the repo's existing validators), clamp all numbers and string lengths, scene coverage validated, emotion ids restricted to the 8. Model output is data, never HTML. Timeouts (AbortSignal) on every external call: Meta, Jev, Blob, Redis, Turnstile. Error responses carry only codes, no internals.
- Errors: stable codes the UI can map, at least: `too_long` (use BYOK), `daily_books_reached` (person cap), `daily_budget_reached` (global cap), `human_required`, `bad_request`, `unavailable`, `not_found`, `expired`.
- Cost logging: record the real Meta+Jev cost per job (tokens and USD, from usage) in job state so we can measure cost per book; expose it in the final step response only as a number for our e2e, nothing else sensitive.

## Tests (mock Meta, Jev, Blob, Redis, Turnstile; no network)
Cover: validation and size limits; caps (2/day per IP or cookie, whichever first; global daily spend reached); refund exactly once on server failure and none on user error; BYOK skips caps and its key never appears in stored job state, Blob writes or logs; cross-site rejected; id regex; step idempotency; model output with bad JSON / out-of-range values / non-taxonomy emotion is rejected or clamped; final payload matches BookPayload shape; expiry.

## Also
- Write the design in `docs/tasks/86-upload-processing.md` (short) per AGENTS.md.
- Add `export const maxDuration` on new routes consistent with Hobby (<= 60).

- Repo: LectorIA-meta (Next.js 16, React 19, vitest). Read AGENTS.md first and follow it.
- Do NOT commit, push, deploy or create branches. Just edit files in this worktree; I review and commit.
- Never read, print or copy .env* files or any secret. Tests must mock Meta, Blob, Redis, Turnstile; no real network calls.
- Never load production music. Do not start dev/prod servers (I do browser checks myself). Don't kill any process you didn't start.
- Keep every file under the repo's size limit (run `npm run check:size`). Split modules if needed.
- UI rules: light mode default, Meta blue #0866FF, never purple. English, warm copy, never the word "Generated". Boxless buttons that still read as clickable. Animate only on hover/click/state change; respect prefers-reduced-motion (no transition under reduce). Keep the string "Bring your own key!" exactly as is.
- Small, focused diff. No unrelated refactors. Add/adjust unit tests for behavior you change.
- Before finishing run: `npm run typecheck`, `npx vitest run`, `npm run check:size`, `npm run check:secrets`. All must pass.
- Final answer: a short summary of what you changed (files) and anything you skipped and why.

+POSTs `{title, author, sections}` to `/api/uploads`, then drives

+`/read/<id>` (`app/home/upload-flow.ts`). The BYOK key travels in the
+`x-byok-key` header on every call and stays in React state; finished
+books land in the localStorage "Your books" list

+reuses the chat/images Turnstile widget when the server asks for it.

+backoff and resume from the server's `done/total`; coded errors map to
+the next step (`too_long`, `daily_books_reached`, `daily_budget_reached`
+open the key step, `human_required` re-asks the check,
+`expired`/`not_found` restart the upload). The free hint allows 2 books
+per UTC day (`core/upload-policy.ts`, `app/home/free-book.ts`); the
+server enforces the real quota.
